purpose: One-factor-at-a-time pilot ablations of complete coupled trajectory optimization; preserve every case and termination status.
rank_policy: Ranks are total space-time ranks. Jacobi uses rank zero. Recycling retains old coarse vectors and a new-direction window equal to the requested rank. Basis, candidate, operator-product and sampled process memory remain separately identified.
starts: Every run starts from the same initial temperature trajectory with empty recycling history. Inner warm starts follow the same optimizer policy. These one-target ablations do not assess reuse across a target sequence.
transfer_scope: The sequential control begins with the same full reference at its first inactive system, then transfers only its previous restricted values at every requested inactive system, including initial-guard returns. It adds no learned or replacement directions. Complete optimizers may take different paths; matched-system replays provide the separate mechanism test.
time_scope: Changing 64 to 32 slabs preserves the 600-second horizon and physical target function. This is a discretization/cost ablation, not a temporal-convergence certificate.
timing: Complete one-target sequence cost includes construction, assembly, all optimizer and inner solves, transfers, original-equation and adjoint verification, telemetry and cleanup. Calibration and process preparation remain separate. Single, potentially concurrent pilots are not final repeated timing measurements.
outcomes: Retain all declared cases, failures, caps, unfinished jobs and unavailable memory samples. Do not report a failed solve as a completed-solve speedup. Follow-up repetitions require a separately frozen design.
gates: A matching computed-flow baseline and derivative verification precede application optimization. The 32-slab group requires its own derivative check. All final residual, nonlinear KKT and conservation criteria remain unchanged.
